chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about the meaning of 'Allah'. So he said: [Allah is] the One Who dominates over whatever is subtle and whatever is great.

key_terms.استولى: To dominate, have sovereignty over, conquer — indicating Allah's comprehensive authority
key_terms.جل: That which is majestic, great, enormous — the manifest realm
key_terms.دق: That which is subtle, minute, fine — the imperceptible realm
key_terms.معنى الله: The meaning/derivation of the name 'Allah', a central theological question

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the name 'Allah' according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) was asked to explain the meaning of the divine name 'Allah'. His response — that Allah is the One Who has dominion over all things, from the most minute to the most majestic — reflects the theological tradition of explaining divine names through their semantic roots. In early Islamic theological discourse, such questions about God's names (asma') were central, and the Imam's answer emphasizes divine omnipotence and sovereignty (istila') as the essential meaning of the name 'Allah'.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the Meaning of ‘Allah’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The One Who Conquers upon whatever is slight and majestic’.
en.sarwar: 3. A group of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Barqi from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hassan ibn Rashid from abul Hassan Musa ibn Ja‘far (a.s.),
who was questioned about the meaning of the word Allah. The Imam replied, “He (Allah) dominates all things small or big.”
